subject: grey cat
title: What If the CIA Turned a Cat Into a Spy? It Did, in the 1960s

scenes.text: What if the CIA turned a cat into a spy? It did, and the first mission lasted minutes.
In an hour-long operation, a vet implanted a microphone in the cat's ear, a transmitter at its skull, and an antenna wire to its tail.
First problem: the cat wandered off whenever it got hungry. So they operated again to fix the hunger.
After years of training, it was driven to a park near the Soviet embassy in Washington and released toward two men.
By the famous account, a taxi hit it almost at once. A former CIA officer later insisted the cat survived.
A 1967 memo closed the project as not practical. Reported cost: up to 20 million dollars, for a cat that never delivered a word.

description:
What if the CIA turned a cat into a listening device? Project Acoustic Kitty did exactly that in the 1960s: a microphone in the ear canal, a transmitter at the base of the skull and an antenna woven through the fur, in an hour-long operation.
The famous story says the cat was run over by a taxi on its first mission outside the Soviet embassy in Washington; a former CIA officer disputes that. Either way a 1967 memo ended the project as not practical, at a reported cost of up to 20 million dollars.

first_comment: The memo did admit that cats can be trained to walk short distances. Which animal would make the worst spy?
